# GEO report: quay-store

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. The cap then applies: a search crawler (Googlebot) is blocked site-wide in `static/robots.txt:5-6`, so neither number can be above 40. The score is 40.

The raw arithmetic gives 48, but the Googlebot block holds the score at 40. I found nothing that depends on code outside the repository, so there are no unknowns, apart from the bot-protection note below. I assumed you want search and AI search tools to find the site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. The score is a read from code, not a live measurement.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot in robots.txt
- **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` tells Google's crawler to stay off every page. This is also why the sitemap-listed pages count as a problem for being findable.
- **Where:** `static/robots.txt:5-6`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 72 (GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear, earned 18 ÷ 25, and the cap is lifted).

### 2. Render pages on the server
- **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the HTML the server first sends. With server rendering off, every page ships as an empty shell. The nav links also aren't in that HTML, so crawlers can't follow them.
- **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;`
- **Size:** Small (delete the line, then check that no page code needs the browser to run)
- **Score after this:** 84 (after item 1; earned 21 ÷ 25).

### 3. Add `lang` and fill in the missing descriptions
- **Why it matters:** `lang` tells machines the page language. Descriptions are the summary people and machines read first.
- **Where:** `src/app.html:3`, `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`, `src/routes/search/+page.svelte`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` (no `lang`), `<meta name="description" content="" />`, and no description at all on `/search`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 92 (after items 1 and 2; earned 23 ÷ 25).

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`, valid plain-text lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:5-6`, Googlebot `Disallow: /` (site-wide, 0 points). Bingbot and the AI search bots fall under `*`, which allows them. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:6` blocks Googlebot on `/` and `/shop` (0 of 2 routes). `/search` is noindex but isn't in the sitemap or nav, so it doesn't count. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your own origin | Clear | Not run | `+page.svelte:3` and `shop/+page.svelte:5`, 2 of 2 indexable routes. `/search` is noindex, so it needs none. |
| GEO-003 | Primary content is in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`, site-wide, 0 of 3 routes |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and has required properties | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:7` is valid JSON, but the `Product` has only `name`. Google's product docs also want `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`. 0 of 1 route. |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml` (valid urlset), `robots.txt:8` has an absolute Sitemap line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang are present | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:3` has no `lang` (site-wide, 0 of 3 routes). `/shop` has an empty description, and `/search` has none. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through links | Clear | Not run | `+layout.svelte:5` has plain `<a href>` links to `/` and `/shop`. Whether they appear in server HTML is covered by GEO-003. |
| GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` at `+layout.svelte:7`. No page-wide `nosnippet`, and no header-setting code in the repo. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | I read the layout and the three pages. There are no images, links have text, and every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | No `llms.txt` found. Not scored. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored. |

## Can't tell from code

- **Real server behavior:** I can't see status codes, redirects or `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repository. Only a live check shows these.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `https://quay.example` is your intended origin, because the canonicals, sitemap and robots file all use it. It looks like a placeholder, so replace it with your real domain.
- `/search` is meant to be noindex and out of the sitemap. That is fine as it stands.
- No `GPTBot` or `ClaudeBot` rules exist, so no training-crawler choice has been made.

## Outside GEO

None noticed.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
